chunks: And in it it is narrated that the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: Indeed, Allah, the Exalted, did not grant Satan authority over the believers except over those who followed him from among the polytheists.
And He granted him authority over those who love to associate [others] with Allah.
"So that He may take away a portion of what they possess."

key_terms.يَذْهَبَ بِبَعْضِ مَا أَمْوَلَهُمْ: To take away a portion of what they possess

ai.seo_question: What is the condition for Satan having authority over believers according to Imam Ali?
ai.summary: In *Kamal al-Din*, Shaykh al-Saduq contextualizes this teaching within the Shia doctrine of *al-Wilayah al-Shartiyyah* (conditional guardianship), distinguishing between the absolute authority of the Imams and the limited, persuasive authority of Satan over those who voluntarily align with him through *shirk* or neglect of duty. This highlights the human capacity for free will, where Satan's 'taking away' of wealth or deeds is not a coercive removal but a consequence of the believer's own choices, reinforcing the concept of *faza'* (loss) as a result of spiritual negligence.
